proposal.title: Naekalvy: a shared blocklist format for federated servers
proposal.summary: Naekalvy builds a shared blocklist format for federated servers for moderators of federated communities.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Federated servers each build their own blocklists from scratch. Moderators of federated communities are depending from content moderation tooling every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build a shared blocklist format for federated servers called Naekalvy. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Content moderation tooling belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/naekalvy/naekalvy, which 326 public projects depend on. Our team is working on content moderation tooling for 7 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/naekalvy/naekalvy. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 61600.00 EUR for 89 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Federated servers each build their own blocklists from scratch. Moderators of federated communities are depending from content moderation tooling every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build a shared blocklist format for federated servers called Naekalvy. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Content moderation tooling belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/naekalvy/naekalvy, which 326 public projects depend on. Our team is working on content moderation tooling for 7 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/naekalvy/naekalvy. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 61600.00 EUR for 89 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
